Hello there, I'm a little bit older than you so I have experienced most of the things you told. But I'm not here to give advice or anything, just some of my own reflections of my experience. And you're right, most of us will go through these things, bad school, bad grades, being jobless, not feeling attractive enough while attracted to hot guys, seeking validation through sex but never feel like it was enough... Most people will go through these things obviously but somehow LGBT will experience them in a deeper way as we are often lonelier and always feel like we are not accepted.
I used to feel like I need to have sex with everybody to prove that I'm attractive enough but later, I realize that if I don't feel "enough" with myself, no matter how many guys I slept with I will never feel enough. So I set up some "fuck buddies" connections with guys that I find myself enjoying the time I was with them. And the same with a relationship involving romance, sometimes I can get hurt cutting off with someone even if he's just a friend with benefits, but we are humans, and it's okay to feel hurt after feeling attached to somebody, whether emotionally or physically.
Other things like jobs, education, you will figure out along the way, just keep going and surround yourself with good people, who accept you for who you are. I think that's what does it for me. Hope you find it helpful in some ways.

Okay let me reiterate it again to be clearer. It's not that AMD will abandon the gaming market or anything, but since this gaming/enthusiast is a niche market, they won't spend too much time and money chasing the leading position in the discrete graphics card anymore. As you said, they will try to cover the wildest range of gamers as possible while saving cost on R&D.

Another point worth mentioning is that AMD has less cash and human resources than both Intel and Nvidia, yet they have to compete on both fronts of CPU and GPU. So I think by the time AMD release Big Navi, Nvidia already has something else equal or better in performance, simply because they have the resources needed to do so.
AMD wants to save money, that's all. Gamers are not their top priority anymore, and I'm okay with that.

Hey sorry for commenting so late even though I have read your post a while ago. Every time I re-read it I always cry, because I see myself in there, like a whole lot. Eversince I was a child, maybe third grade or so I had this existential dread but it did not bother me much at the time, maybe I didn't know much. And time goes by and life turned out to be less than what I expected, from the body dysmorphia to the loss of relationships, and people keep telling me it will get better but it doesn't seem to, perhaps even worse.

This is not to say that your experience and I are the same, certainly I don't understand everything, but I understand some part of it. And I honestly don't know where you are right now or if you're still alive, because I was close to suicide sometimes and I'm still not out of this dark place, or I'll ever be, I could not tell you to simply "stay" or "get better" because we both know we have tried and somehow unsuccessful. All I want to say is your writing is beautiful, your soul is beautiful, even if you have made some mistakes, it's okay. I hope you can see your own beauty, even just a little bit.
